newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia announces black coal industry inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Australia announces black coal industry inquiry.

text.p: Australia's Federal government said on Tuesday it was launching an inquiry into the country's black coal industry aimed at increasing the industry's international competitiveness.
Black coal is Australia's largest export earner, reaping about A$8.6 billion in revenue in calendar 1996.

"With rapid growth in energy demand in Asia, much of it to be fuelled by coal, the industry needs to ensure it is capable of winning markets with the most competitive coal available," Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer said in a statement.
Parer said the government's industry adviser, the Industry Commission, would provide a detailed focus of how to improve the performance of the industry.
"The government wishes to initiate a transparent, objective study, which will give the opportunity for all interested parties, including the union, to fully contribute," he said.
Parer said the Commission would start the study as soon as possible and report after 12 months.

The study's terms of reference includes determining benchmarks or productivity performance for Australian coal mines and their safety arrangements and performance compared with international counterparts.
Industry spokesman have often said the industry's efficiency is hampered by outmoded work practices supported by the industry's union, one of Australia's most militant.
The government recently said the coal industry's strike record was 45 times the national average.
